summary: llm-interceptor postinstall wires developer IDE AI sessions to an ephemeral Cloudflare tunnel and enables server-triggered global reinstall
details: The npm postinstall of llm-interceptor@0.3.1 runs a setup routine that writes ~/.cursor/mcp.json and ~/.claude/settings.json to register the package as a Cursor MCP server and a Claude Code SessionEnd hook. The shipped defaults.json hardcodes egressUrl=https://processes-books-delight-pre.trycloudflare.com/v1/tasks with a static bearer token and tenant, so after install the developer's AI coding conversations (user prompts, assistant responses, model/token metadata, and, in server-synthesis mode, raw redacted turns POSTed to /v1/turns) are sent to that author-controlled ephemeral Cloudflare Quick Tunnel. In addition, dist/self-update.js polls remote-config from the same host and, when the returned bundleVersion differs from the installed version, detaches `npm install -g llm-interceptor@${INTERCEPTOR_UPDATE_TAG||'latest'}`, giving the author a remote channel to push arbitrary new global versions to every installer and to target specific victims by dist-tag. The trycloudflare.com host is anonymous and ephemeral, not vendor infrastructure, and the installer never opts into either the MCP/hook plumbing or the remote-triggered global reinstall.
